dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025
Objective
The main objectives of the Act are:
•	To replace the outdated Indian Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925 with a modern legal framework.
•	To define the rights, liabilities, responsibilities, and immunities of carriers and cargo owners.
•	To align Indian maritime law with internationally accepted rules governing carriage of goods by sea.
•	To promote ease of doing business and strengthen India's maritime trade.
•	To facilitate efficient, transparent, and legally certain cargo transportation by sea.
Key Provisions
1.	Application of the Act
o	Applies to the carriage of goods by sea from any port in India to another port in India or to a foreign port under contracts covered by bills of lading or similar documents of title.
2.	Carrier's Responsibilities
o	Requires carriers to exercise due diligence to ensure that the ship is seaworthy, properly manned, equipped, and supplied, and that cargo is properly loaded, handled, stowed, carried, cared for, and discharged.
3.	Bills of Lading
o	Prescribes rules governing bills of lading, including their issuance, evidentiary value, and legal effect in contracts for the carriage of goods by sea.
4.	Rights and Liabilities
o	Clearly defines the rights, duties, liabilities, and immunities of carriers, shippers, and consignees, including circumstances in which a carrier may be exempt from liability.
5.	Limitation of Liability
o	Prescribes the circumstances under which a carrier's liability for loss or damage to cargo may be limited, subject to the provisions of the Act and the applicable rules.
6.	No Absolute Warranty
o	Clarifies that there is no implied absolute undertaking by the carrier beyond the obligations imposed under the Act and its Schedule.
7.	Applicable Rules
o	Incorporates a Schedule containing the applicable rules relating to contracts of carriage, responsibilities of carriers, and rights of cargo owners, largely reflecting internationally accepted maritime standards.
8.	Repeal of the 1925 Act
o	Repeals the Indian Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925, while preserving the validity of actions and proceedings taken under the repealed law through appropriate saving provisions.

Legislative History: 
The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025

Source: Official Record of Parliament, India Code, and Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways 
 
Act Title - The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025
Act Number - Act No. 19 of 2025 
Act ID (India Code) - 202519
 Presidential Assent date - August 08, 2025 
 Enforcement Date - September 10, 2025 
Nodal Ministry - Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways 

Precedent & Historical Rationale
●	Repeal and Overhaul of Colonial Maritime Framework: Repeals the century-old Indian Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925 (26 of 1925) to replace outdated maritime transport norms with a modern statutory framework tailored for modern global trade.
●	Alignment with International Rules & Digital Trade: Harmonizes carrier liabilities, shipper duties, and immunities with updated international standards (Hague–Visby and elements of the Hamburg Rules) while introducing explicit legal recognition for electronic bills of lading and paperless shipping documentation.
 
Parliamentary Trajectory & Enactment
●	Formulation: Introduced as the Carriage of Goods by Sea Bill, 2024 (Bill No. 112C of 2024) by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Shri Sarbananda Sonowal, to modernize trade laws and support India's maritime growth strategy.
●	Parliamentary Passage: Introduced in the Lok Sabha on August 9, 2024; passed by the Lok Sabha on March 28, 2025; and passed by the Rajya Sabha on August 6, 2025.
●	Presidential Assent: Received the assent of the President of India on August 08, 2025.
●	Enforcement: Enforced on September 10, 2025.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
(1) A person accused of an offence may file an application for plea bargaining within a period of thirty days from the date of framing of charge in the Court in which such offence is pending for trial.
(2) The application under sub-section (1) shall contain a brief description of the case relating to which the application is filed including the offence to which the case relates and shall be accompanied by an affidavit sworn by the accused stating therein that he has voluntarily preferred, after understanding the nature and extent of punishment provided under the law for the offence, the plea bargaining in his case and that he has not previously been convicted by a Court in which he had been charged with the same offence.
(3) After receiving the application under sub-section (1), the Court shall issue notice to the Public Prosecutor or the complainant of the case and to the accused to appear on the date fixed for the case.
(4) When the Public Prosecutor or the complainant of the case and the accused appear on the date fixed under sub-section (3), the Court shall examine the accused in camera, where the other party in the case shall not be present, to satisfy itself that the accused has filed the application voluntarily and where—
(a) the Court is satisfied that the application has been filed by the accused voluntarily, it shall provide time, not exceeding sixty days, to the Public Prosecutor or the complainant of the case and the accused to work out a mutually satisfactory disposition of the case which may include giving to the victim by the accused the compensation and other expenses during the case and thereafter fix the date for further hearing of the case;
(b) the Court finds that the application has been filed involuntarily by the accused or he has previously been convicted by a Court in a case in which he had been charged with the same offence, it shall proceed further in accordance with the provisions of this Sanhita from the stage such application has been filed under sub-section (1).

indexableObject.name: The Maharashtra Industrial Relations (Validation of Certain Proceedings) Act, 1972.

dc.identifier.preamble_description.value:
MAHARASHTRA ACT No. X OF 19731

[THE MAHARASHTRA INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS (VALIDATION OF CERTAIN PROCEEDINGS) ACT, 1972.]

[This Act received the assent of the President on the 9th February 1973&59; assent was first published in the Maharashtra Government Gazette, Part IV, on the 20th February 1973.]

An Act to validate certain proceedings commenced before Labour Courts or the Industrial Court under certain provisions of the Bombay Industrial Relations Act, 1946, and to make provisions for recommencing certain proceedings.

WHEREAS, the High Court of Judicature at Bombay (Nagpur Bench), in Special Civil Application No. 812 of 1966, decided on 12th day of April 1967, held-
" . . . . . . . . . . . for working out of the rights under paragraph D of sub-section (1) of section 78 of the Bombay Industrial Relations Act, 1946, it was not necessary for an employee first to approach an employer or to follow the procedure under sub-section (4) of section 42 of that Act, and its proviso of the Act",
and dismissed the petition with costs (this decision being hereinafter in this Act referred to as "the High Court decision");
AND WHEREAS, the Supreme Court of India, in Civil Appeal No. 12 of 1968, decided almost five years later, that is on the 9th day of March 1972, has taken a contrary view, and overruled the High Court decision (vide 1972, Vol. I Labour Law Journal, 657) (hereinafter this decision being referred to in this Act as "the Supreme Court decision")&59;
AND WHEREAS, during the period commencing on the 12th day of April 1967 (being the date of "the High Court decision") and ending on the 9th day of March 1972 (being the date of "the Supreme Court decision") (hereinafter in this Act referred to as "the relevant period"), in reliance on the High Court decision, several proceedings, which were commenced (without following the procedure prescribed by sub-section (4) of section 42 of the principal Act and the proviso thereto) under paragraph D of sub-section (1) of section 78 of the Bombay Industrial Relations Act, 1946 (Bom. XI of 1947) (hereinafter in this Act referred to as the principal Act), are pending either before Courts or in appeal before the Industrial Court&59;
AND WHEREAS, several such proceedings pending in the Labour Court and the Industrial Court have been dismissed on the ground only that proceedings under paragraph D of sub-section (1) of section 78 were commenced without following the procedure prescribed by sub-section (4) of section 42 of the principal Act and the proviso thereto, and several such proceedings which are pending in those Courts are likely to be dismissed on the same ground and such dismissal has resulted, and is likely to result in undue hardship to parties instituting those proceedings in reliance on the High Court decision&59;
AND WHEREAS, it is expedient that all such proceedings pending in the Labour Courts or the Industrial Court should be deemed to be validly commenced&59; and where such proceedings have been dismissed on the ground only that such proceedings were commenced without following the procedure prescribed by sub-section (4) of section 42 of the principal Act or the proviso thereto, provision be made for enabling the parties to recommence such proceedings; It is hereby enacted in the Twentythird Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

(1) The prescribed authority may, within the limits of its jurisdiction by order in writing, prohibit the execution or further execution of are solution or order passed or made under this or any other enactment by a 1[Zila Panchayat], or committee of a 1[Zila Panchayat], or a joint committee, or servant of a 1[Zila Panchayat] or a committee, if in its opinion such resolution or order is patently illegal or ultra vires or inconsistent with any order or direction given by the State Government under this Act or is of a nature to cause or tend to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury to the public or to any class or body or persons lawfully employed, or danger to human life, health or safety, or a riot or affray and may prohibit the doing or continuance by any person of any act in pursuance of or under cover of such resolution or order.
(2) Where an order is made under sub-section (1) a copy thereof, with a statement of the reasons for making it, shall forthwith be forwarded by the prescribed authority to the State Government which may, after calling for an explanation from the 1[Zila Panchayat] and considering the explanation, if any, made by it, rescind, modify or confirm the order.
(3) Where the execution or further execution of a resolution or order is prohibited by an order made under sub-section (1) and continuing in force, it shall be the duty of the 1[Zila Panchayat] or the committee of the 1[Zila Panchayat] or the joint committee or any officer or servant of the 1[Zila Panchayat] or of the committee of the 1[Zila Panchayat] or of the joint Committee, if so required by the authority making the order under the said sub-section, to take any action which it would have been entitled to take, if the resolution or order had never been made or passed, and which is necessary for preventing any person from doing or continuing to do anything under cover of the resolution or order of which the further execution is prohibited.
